awards.epitaph: 4 Winds Wrestling ran one full awards season, gathering nominations by e-mail through November 2004 and putting the top two in each category on a hosted ballot. Its own Wrestler of the Year for 2004 was Darek DeAngelo.

bestowals.vote_detail: Nominated: Joey Malone, LLB, The Elements and Simon Seaman.
bestowals.source: Action Wrestling's own Action! Awards of 13 March 2003, its first annual ceremony (/promotions/action-2002/archive/action-2002-the-action-awards-2003-2003-03-13.html): “Action Wrestling’s best Champion thus far… LLB.” and the scene closes “Winner: LLB.”

bestowals.vote_detail: Nominated: Jeff Garvin, LLB, Max Danger and Syphon Fission.
bestowals.source: Action Wrestling's own Action! Awards of 13 March 2003, its first annual ceremony (/promotions/action-2002/archive/action-2002-the-action-awards-2003-2003-03-13.html): “The winner is Jeff Garvin.” and the scene closes “Winner: Jeff Garvin.” His own card reads “A! Heel of the Year” (/promotions/action-2002/archive/jeff-garvin-bio.html).

bestowals.vote_detail: Announced for LLB's Erroneous Conclusion; both men walked up and LLB handed Coral Avalon the trophy.
bestowals.source: Action Wrestling's own Action! Awards of 13 March 2003, its first annual ceremony (/promotions/action-2002/archive/action-2002-the-action-awards-2003-2003-03-13.html): the envelope names “The ‘Erroneous Conclusion’!”, LLB and Coral Avalon both come to the stage, LLB says “but I’m the winner of the move” and hands Avalon the award, and the results line reads “Winner: LLB and Coral Avalon?” Filed as a shared award, in that order.

bestowals.vote_detail: Joey Malone and Syphon Fission, over LLB/KroW, Malone/Kent Anthason and LLB/Christopher Fox.
bestowals.source: Action Wrestling's own Action! Awards of 13 March 2003, its first annual ceremony (/promotions/action-2002/archive/action-2002-the-action-awards-2003-2003-03-13.html): “Joey Malone and Syphon Fission!” and the scene closes “Winners: Joey Malone & Syphon Fission.” Malone's card reads “Feud of the Year(w/ Fission)” and Fission's “2003 Feud of the Year(w/Joey Malone)” — his card's year differs from the ceremony's first annual year, and both are as written (/promotions/action-2002/archive/joey-malone-action-2002-bio.html; /promotions/action-2002/archive/syphon-fission-action-2002-bio.html).

bestowals.vote_detail: Cylear's return at Last Laugh, over the Objection/Erection birth, the Scout Hat confrontation and The Truth Is Told.
bestowals.source: Action Wrestling's own Action! Awards of 13 March 2003, its first annual ceremony (/promotions/action-2002/archive/action-2002-the-action-awards-2003-2003-03-13.html): the presenter opens the envelope — “And the winner of this award is… Sean Cylear’s return to Action!” — Cylear accepts in a speech and the scene closes “Winner: Sean Cylear.” The nominations are four clips, not persons.

bestowals.vote_detail: “LLB's Not a Lawyer” (Blood, Sweat, Tears) over Keri's turn on her husband, Cylear's return and KroW leaving.
bestowals.source: Action Wrestling's own Action! Awards of 13 March 2003, its first annual ceremony (/promotions/action-2002/archive/action-2002-the-action-awards-2003-2003-03-13.html): “And the winner is… LLB’s not a lawyer!” LLB accepts and the scene closes “Winner: LLB.” The award is for the moment; it is filed to LLB, who stands at its centre and accepts it.

bestowals.vote_detail: Nominated: Keri Lindum, Reed Young, Siobhan Tyler and Pikachu.
bestowals.source: Action Wrestling's own Action! Awards of 13 March 2003, its first annual ceremony (/promotions/action-2002/archive/action-2002-the-action-awards-2003-2003-03-13.html): the envelope is opened — “And the winner iiissssss… Um. Keri Lindum slash Malone?” — and the scene closes “Winner: Keri Lindum.” Her own card gives the year as “Manager of the Year(2002-2003)” (/promotions/action-2002/archive/keri-lindum-action-2002-bio.html); the ceremony itself is the first annual one, filed under 2002.

bestowals.vote_detail: The Iron Man Match, Coral Avalon vs Jeff Garvin at Players and Pawns, over seven other nominated matches.
bestowals.source: Action Wrestling's own Action! Awards of 13 March 2003, its first annual ceremony (/promotions/action-2002/archive/action-2002-the-action-awards-2003-2003-03-13.html): “…And the winner’s ARE… CORAL AVALON! JEFF GARVIN! THE IRON MAN MATCH!” and the scene closes “Winners: Coral Avalon & Jeff Garvin.” Their own cards read “Match of the Year(vs. Jeff Garvin @ Players & Pawns)” and “A! Match of the Year (w/ Coral Avalon)” (/promotions/action-2002/archive/coral-avalon-acw-bio.html; /promotions/action-2002/archive/jeff-garvin-bio.html).

bestowals.vote_detail: Nominated: Coral Avalon, Max Danger, Keith Scott Zimmerman and Conrad Ramsey.
bestowals.source: Action Wrestling's own Action! Awards of 13 March 2003, its first annual ceremony (/promotions/action-2002/archive/action-2002-the-action-awards-2003-2003-03-13.html): “And the winner is, drum roll please… MAX DANGER!” and the scene closes “Winner: Max Danger.” The scene's header names four nominees and the voice-over reads six (adding Jeff Garvin and Bobby Minio); both are as it stands.

bestowals.vote_detail: Players and Pawns won over Juggernaut, Til Death and D4TC; the presenter, Sanchis Su Idolo, walked off with the trophy.
bestowals.source: Action Wrestling's own Action! Awards of 13 March 2003, its first annual ceremony (/promotions/action-2002/archive/action-2002-the-action-awards-2003-2003-03-13.html): the presenter opens the envelope, reads “Players & Pawns!?” and the scene closes “Winner: Players and Pawns.” The winner is a card, not a wrestler, so no recipient is filed. His own biography card lists it among his Fed Awards, wryly: “PPV of the Year(well, okay, he STOLE the award…)” (/promotions/action-2002/archive/sanchissu-idolo-action-2002-bio.html).

bestowals.vote_detail: Three named for enrolment in the Ring of Gold, the company's own hall of fame, once they retire from it.
bestowals.source: Action Wrestling's own Action! Awards of 13 March 2003, its first annual ceremony (/promotions/action-2002/archive/action-2002-the-action-awards-2003-2003-03-13.html): “The Ring of Gold Nominees are Joey Malone, LLB, and Christopher Fox.” and the scene closes “Nominated: Joey Malone, LLB & Christopher Fox.” The scene itself says the three would be up for enrolment “when retired from AW”; this is a nomination for a later honour, not an induction, and none is filed.

bestowals.vote_detail: Nominated: Reed Young, Jeremy Bold, Pringles the Puppy and a joke nominee.
bestowals.source: Action Wrestling's own Action! Awards of 13 March 2003, its first annual ceremony (/promotions/action-2002/archive/action-2002-the-action-awards-2003-2003-03-13.html): the envelope is opened and the winner is “my daddy, Reed Young”, the presenter being his son; the scene closes “Winner: Reed Young.” His own card reads “Owner of the best, Fed, EEEVVVEEERRR!!” (/promotions/action-2002/archive/reed-young-action-2002-bio.html).

bestowals.vote_detail: Nominated: Winds of Change, Clit 'N Candy, Pretty Fly and The Elements; Action! Team accepted for them.
bestowals.source: Action Wrestling's own Action! Awards of 13 March 2003, its first annual ceremony (/promotions/action-2002/archive/action-2002-the-action-awards-2003-2003-03-13.html): “And the winners are… the Elements!”, the team not being present, and the scene closes “Winners: The Elements.”

bestowals.vote_detail: Nominated: Joey Malone, LLB, Coral Avalon and Christopher Fox.
bestowals.source: Action Wrestling's own Action! Awards of 13 March 2003, its first annual ceremony (/promotions/action-2002/archive/action-2002-the-action-awards-2003-2003-03-13.html): a guest presenter opens the sheet — “The winner is… Christopher Fox…” — and the scene closes “Winner: Christopher Fox.” His own card reads “Top Face 2002-2003” (/promotions/action-2002/archive/christopher-fox-action-2002-bio.html).

bestowals.vote_detail: Nominated: LLB, Christopher Fox, Joey Malone and Airborn Tyler.
bestowals.source: Action Wrestling's own Action! Awards of 13 March 2003, its first annual ceremony (/promotions/action-2002/archive/action-2002-the-action-awards-2003-2003-03-13.html): “And this year’s wrestler of the year… the very first in Action Wrestling… Joey Malone.” and the scene closes “Winner: Joey Malone.” His own card reads “Wrestler of the Year” (/promotions/action-2002/archive/joey-malone-action-2002-bio.html).

Nothing held documents any induction after November 2000.

awards.name: EWA Innovation Championship
awards.epitaph: A championship that exists because Ryan Shane declared it into being on Shatter Point in July 2011 — pulling an unseen belt from Ms. Fontaine's velvet bag and naming himself the most innovative man in the sport before anyone else had a say. Ronnie McNeil took exception on the spot, snatched the belt from him, and threw it back in his face without ever being counted a champion for it.
awards.notes: Ryan Shane produced the belt himself out of a velvet bag on Shatter Point 7/5/11 and crowned himself the first champion on the spot; no sanctioning by EWA's own front office is recorded.

bestowals.vote_detail: Self-awarded on Shatter Point 7/5/11; no sanctioning by EWA's own front office is recorded. Ronnie McNeil snatched the belt from him minutes later and threw it back in his face without being counted a champion for it.

awards.name: Joe Smallze Memorial Cup
awards.epitaph: A cup FAW gave in memory of Joe “Soulja” Smallze, who wrestled here and died in April 2002. One holder survives in the record: Tony Vigilante, introduced on the 10 August 2003 Panic as “the Joe Smallze 2003 memorial cup holder”. Nothing else in the surviving record describes how it was contested or who else ever held it. It is the second thing FAW named for him — the fed retired its Television Championship unfilled in his name the year before.

bestowals.source: FAW's own Panic recap of 10 August 2003 (promotions/faw/archive/panic-2003-08-10.html) — the ring announcer's own introduction: “he is the Joe Smallze 2003 memorial cup holder and number one contender to the FAW World Heavyweight Championship... Mr. Tony Vigilante!!!” A second source, nine days earlier: FAW’s own Panic preview of 1 August 2003, carried on eWNews (promotions/ew-news-2002/news/panic-preview-08-03-2003-2003-08-01.html), names the runner-up — Spawn, “more than displeased since losing the Joe Smallze Memorial Cup to Tony Vigilante in the Final.”

bestowals.vote_detail: 31%, the World Title Cage Match — a three-way tie for third at 23% each (Studog Escobar, Twiztid, the Dark Lords, Team Esco, Nephilim, Ace Thunder); no second place recorded in the ceremony's own recap table. The ceremony's own script names the match "the World Title Cage Match at Fear the Raine"; the following year's ceremony instead calls the same pairing's win a match "at March Maelstrom II" — the two GIWF ceremony scripts disagree with each other on the event name, not just with any outside source; recorded as an open discrepancy between two primary documents rather than silently resolved. CORRECTED from an earlier registry entry that credited the-phenomenons here, sourced only from a later, self-attested Hall of Fame induction boast. The actual GIWF ceremony transcript — a live, contemporary primary source — settles it: the Phenomenons placed in that three-way tie for third at 23%, not first. See giwf-2000-match-of-the-year's own provenance note for where the Phenomenons' real Match of the Year win actually landed.

bestowals.vote_detail: 47.06%, Venetian Home Rumble I — the Phenomenons vs. Al Crud & the joke gimmick Tom the Christmas Tree, fought at Christmas Clash '99 — over Slasher/CA$H's THC Title War (23.53%), the Nightmare Reflections Match (17.65%), and Al Crud/Pete Steele's Regal Rumble main event (11.76%). PROVENANCE NOTE, resolving a dating discrepancy: a Phenomenons Hall of Fame induction speech elsewhere self-attests a "1999 GIWF Match of the Year" win for this same Venetian Home Rumble; the actual match happened at a Dec 1999 show, but the GIWF's own annual-awards cycle crowned it at the ceremony covering "year 2000" (the 1999 ceremony's own Match of the Year, held only weeks earlier, had already gone to Curt Raines & Hamish McGrubber — see giwf-1999-match-of-the-year). Read together, the two contemporary ceremony transcripts show the HOF speech's own claim as misdated by one ceremony cycle, not fabricated: right match, wrong year named. Both rows stand, each receipted to its own ceremony's own primary transcript. Independently corroborated by a later UWF retrospective ("the battle... that had won the 2000 Match of the Year award") and a Christmas Clash 2000 preview calling Rumble I the favorite for the award.

awards.name: Universal Tag Team Titles (self-awarded)
awards.epitaph: A foam belt, never a sanctioned GIWF championship, that the Phenomenons gave themselves and wore in-character as though it outranked their six real title reigns — three times World Tag Team Champions, three times North American — yet left off the Accomplishments in their own GIWF bio. When Deke Aurora and Nephilim snatched the belts at ringside on 29 August 1999, a new pair from the GIWF catalogue arrived three days later; no one else ever claimed the title: it was always just theirs.
awards.notes: Source: the Phenomenons' own GIWF bio page, which describes each man as “always” wearing his “Universal Tag Team Title belt”; and the GIWF's own cards, where the belts appear from Suicide of 29 August 1999 to Global of 1 August 2001.

bestowals.vote_detail: Given by the Phenomenons to themselves: GIWF merchandise foam belts trimmed in gold, which the two of them wore to the ring as the Universal Tag Team Titles and billed above their real championships. On the fed's own cards from 29 August 1999 to 1 August 2001; no date of the self-awarding itself survives.
bestowals.source: The GIWF's own cards, among them Suicide of 29 August 1999 (promotions/giwf/archive/suicide-1999-08-29.html: "They carry round Foam belts with gold trim and you recognise those as genuine universal tag-team straps?????"), Quake of 30 September 1999 (promotions/giwf/archive/quake.html: "GIWF Merchandising foam belts decorated with gold leaf and declare themselves to be the Universal Tag Team champions"), Global of 6 July 2000 (promotions/giwf/archive/global-2000-07-06.html: "the current GIWF Universal Tag Team Champions") and Global of 1 August 2001 (promotions/giwf/archive/global-2001-08-01.html); and the Phenomenons' own GIWF bio page, which describes each man as "always" wearing his "Universal Tag Team Title belt".

bestowals.vote_detail: Shared. Seymour Almasy and Saij tied on 13 votes each of the 43 cast, and were declared co-holders of the award. Argyle took nominations by private message through November 2004 ("Character, not handler"; one to three picks, each with reasons), short-listed the five characters nominated more than once, and counted a private ballot sent to him by private message. Third was AWS Man (also known as Bill), then Jason Hughes, then Chris Storm. Each winner was promised a splash image in the site's random rotation.
bestowals.source: PTC forum, Announcements: "Winner - Ptc Wrestler Of The Year..." (topic 11833, post 124777, Argyle, 19 Dec 2004: "Winner, the 2004 PTC Wrestler of the Year: Seymour Almasy and Saij, with 13 votes a piece. Thus, they are co-holders of the award. Total votes, 43."); "PTC Wrestler of the Year Shortlist - 5 Candidates!" (topic 11530, post 121714, 3 Dec 2004); E-Wrestling: "PTC's 2004 Wrestler of the Year" (topic 10886, post 112864, 2 Nov 2004, the call for nominations). PTCpedia's own PTC Wrestler of the Year page (/promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-ptc-wrestler-of-the-year.html, captured 7 Mar 2008): "2004 Seymour Almasy and Saij tied scores in a public ballot." Also cited in commentary on the UWF's Contest of Champions 3 (promotions/uwf/archive/contest-of-champions-3-2005.html: "the co-PTC wrestler of the year").

bestowals.vote_detail: Chosen from 21 self-nominated characters by a ballot sent privately to Argyle, each vote required to give reasons including at least one feat the nominee had not listed; voting closed at midnight on 31 December 2005. Deville put his own case forward on the forum's 2005 nomination thread on 9 December 2005, and the result was billed for PTC Radio's first 2006 edition, in mid-January 2006. Fellow nominee Rich Rollins campaigned for the award in character with a hype video, posted on 30 December 2005 and re-uploaded to YouTube in 2007 as "PTC WOTY 2005 Rollins"; its claim of the award for Rollins is his own campaign's, and the ballot went to Deville.
bestowals.source: PTCpedia's own PTC Wrestler of the Year page (/promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-ptc-wrestler-of-the-year.html): "2005 Angelo Deville won a public ballot." PTC forum, E-Wrestling, post 178618 (the nomination, 9 Dec 2005); Technology, post 185492 (Argyle, 4 Feb 2006: "Angelo Deville - PTC 2005 Wrestler of the Year"); Administration, post 188298 (Rich Rollins, PTC Global Champion, in character, 27 Feb 2006: "the 2005 Wrestler of the Year in Angelo Deville"). The ballot: E-Wrestling, "PTC Wrestler of the Year - 2005!  Stage 2 enclosed - VOTE NOW" (topic 16449, post 181159, Argyle, 24 Dec 2005: the 21 nominees and the voting rules); Announcements, "PTC Radio 2006 Edition 1 coming this Saturday night" (topic 16602, post 183149, 13 Jan 2006: "Tune in for: - 2005 Wrestler of the Year"); E-Wrestling, "PTC Wrestler of the Year 2007 - Nominations" (topic 22110, post 255544, Argyle, 2 Dec 2007: "previous WOTY winners the likes of Chryste (2003), Seymour Almasy and Saij (2004) and Angelo Deville (2005)"; "Rollins and Deville juiced it up for this in 2005, including making videos"). Rollins's video: PTC's Infinite Gauntlet, "The One Hype (PTC 2005 WOTY Nomination Hype Video)" (topic 16499, post 181774, 30 Dec 2005), re-uploaded to YouTube as "PTC WOTY 2005 Rollins" (video lKAGZauXcn4, uploaded 5 Dec 2007; its description: "This used to be on zippyvideos.").

bestowals.vote_detail: The first PTC Wrestler of the Year, decided by members' vote in the 2003 PTC Awards; by her own count, she took 11 votes, one more than double the runner-up's. The award earned her a splash image in the site's random rotation.
bestowals.source: PTCpedia's own PTC Wrestler of the Year page (/promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-ptc-wrestler-of-the-year.html, captured 7 Mar 2008): "2003 Chryste won a public ballot." PTC forum, E-Wrestling: "PTC accomplishments" (topic 1238, post 11966, 17 Nov 2003, her own list of her PTC honours: "Wrestler of the Year (2003) With 11 votes (Double + 1 of Second place)"); "PTC's 2004 Wrestler of the Year" (topic 10886, post 112864, Argyle, 2 Nov 2004: the prize is a splash "similar to the one Chryste has acknowledging winning of the 2003 WOTY award"); E-Wrestling, "PTC Wrestler of the Year 2007 - Nominations" (topic 22110, post 255544, Argyle, 2 Dec 2007): "Chryste (2003)".

bestowals.vote_detail: No official award. Self-nominations opened on 16 February 2007 and closed at the end of that month; Argyle later wrote that there was no official 2006 Wrestler of the Year because the nominations were too few and too thin, and that Doctor Curiosity's handler "ended up awarding it to himself". Doctor Curiosity crowned himself PTC Wrestler of the Year 2006 in character on 2 May 2007, and PTCpedia carries him as the unofficial winner. Tchu disputed the claim in character in December 2007.
bestowals.source: PTCpedia's own PTC Wrestler of the Year page (/promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-ptc-wrestler-of-the-year.html, captured 7 Mar 2008): "2006 No contest due to lack of effort. Unoffficial winner is Doctor Curiosity." PTC forum, E-Wrestling: "2006 Wrestler of the Year - Nominate Yourself Here" (topic 20195, post 225308, 16 Feb 2007); E-Wrestling, "PTC Wrestler of the Year 2007 - Nominations" (topic 22110, post 255544, Argyle, 2 Dec 2007): "We didn't have an official 2006 Wrestler of the year because the number of nominations received and the effort put into those was... lacklustre"; PTC's Infinite Gauntlet: "Wrestler of 'The Year'" (topic 20643, post 229101, 2 May 2007, Doctor Curiosity's own in-character crowning); "Is the Doctor in? 2006 WotY" (topic 22137, post 255853, Tchu, 7 Dec 2007).

bestowals.vote_detail: Nominations by private message to Argyle opened on 2 December 2007. No winner was declared: PTCpedia, captured in March 2008, gives 2007 as "To be determined". Clinton Sage's own handler posted on 28 March 2008 that Clinton Sage and Jason Snow "swept the votes", and in May 2008 that the two had "'unofficially' tied" for the award; that claim is his own.
bestowals.source: E-Wrestling, "PTC Wrestler of the Year 2007 - Nominations" (topic 22110, post 255544, Argyle, 2 Dec 2007); PTCpedia's own PTC Wrestler of the Year page (/promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-ptc-wrestler-of-the-year.html, captured 7 Mar 2008): "2007 To be determined." E-Wrestling: "What's new" (topic 22796, post 262435, 28 Mar 2008: "Clinton Sage and Jason Snow swept the votes for 2007 PTC Wrestler of the Year. Swept."); "Just one ..." (topic 23074, post 265368, 6 May 2008: "the PTC 2007 Wrestler of the Year award that we've 'unofficially' tied for").

The served results list every entrant who drew two or more votes; only the winners are minted here, and the document itself is the ledger of the rest.

awards.name: Top 200
awards.epitaph: The rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll, counted every January and posted back to the group: two hundred wrestlers placed in order, with a written entry for the top twenty-five in most years. Eight editions survive, ranking 1996 through 2004, and the compiler of the first two cross-referenced them himself — the 1997 edition names a wrestler's 1996 place thirty-two times, twice getting the number wrong. What the poll is worth now is not the order it put people in but the census it took by accident: 1,610 placings, and in every year but the first, each one tagged with the federation the wrestler was writing for.

awards.name: Top 200 Tag Teams
awards.epitaph: A tag-team companion to the newsgroup's own singles poll, run under the same house rules by the same compiler in at least three editions (1997-1999); only the 1998 edition survives in the held record, and only in part — the newsgroup's own two release posts cover its lower ninety-nine placings (#99 down to #1) with a written entry for the top twenty-five, the same format the singles Top 200 used for its own top twenty-five. The upper hundred spots (#200-#100) are not recovered.

awards.name: Top 75
awards.notes: The newsgroup’s first community ranking of its own wrestlers, a year before the poll that became the Top 200 and built by a different method: a survey of the federations rather than a ballot of readers, topped up from whatever rankings the federations that did not answer had posted to the newsgroup themselves. Billed as an attempt at a top 100 and stopped at 75 for want of data, in the compiler’s own words.

awards.epitaph: WIA’s own staff ranked its top ten wrestlers with a paragraph of commentary apiece — praising roleplays, noting who’d stepped up and who was still waiting to debut. One clean edition survives whole, dated January 2003. A second, undated Top 10 sidebar survives on the fed’s own later news/front page (Wayback-captured 26 March 2003, bounded no earlier than 20 January 2003): eight names carry over, Spastic and AAH drop out, and David Valdez and Hunter Tazi appear for the first time — consistent with Spastic’s own move from wrestler to owner on 26 January — but nothing dates that second list precisely enough to ledger it as its own year-bestowal alongside the first, so it stands as prose here rather than a second row.
